content:
Harper: flagging an odd resume-accept race we saw this morning on canary. Clients sometimes see slight reorder + duplicate small events after a scale action. Repro is easy with multiplexed clients.
Lin: can you paste a trace? rough suspicion: resume acceptance not strictly atomic during fast route flips.
Harper: logs from one session:```
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] client_disconnect token=rt-332 reason=net-err
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] router: migrate session=s-42 -> node=eu-c-7
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] node=eu-c-6 accept_resume token=rt-332 session=s-42
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] node=eu-c-7 accept_resume token=rt-332 session=s-42
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] node=eu-c-7 emit evt=301 sess=s-42
[2026-04-08T07:45:02Z] client_recv evt=301
[2026-04-08T07:45:03Z] node=eu-c-6 emit evt=300 sess=s-42
[2026-04-08T07:45:03Z] client_recv evt=300
```
Harper: both nodes accepted the same resume token nearly simultaneously; client sees 301 then 300. Not huge window but breaks client-side ordering assumptions.
Gina: was there a change to resume acceptance TTL or the routing fast-path recently?
Lin: yes we shipped runtime/routing/2026-04-07/fast-handoff to reduce tail. It relaxed exclusivity to avoid retries. That likely created a tiny dual-accept window.
Mika (console): console telemetry shows "active_streams" briefly spiking and a new support ticket about ordering. We should show a short note on route pages while we triage.
Harper: quick mitigation options: 1) short-term revert for canary, 2) add strict-accept for mpx sessions only (single-writer lock for resumes), 3) server-side dedupe buffer so duplicate event emissions are dropped at delivery plane, 4) console annotation + metric to track resume_overlap.
Lin: strict single-writer is clean correctness but increases handoff latency and could lead to more drops under packet loss. Dedupe buffer is low-risk and addresses billing duplicates, but doesn't fix ordering.
Gina: what's the billing risk? ops-bot?
ops-bot: alert: billing_inflate risk when duplicates > 0.1% in last 5m. Current sampled sessions show small duplicates. Billing dedupe by (resume_token,event_id) for 10s is possible but may not catch all SDK replays.
Harper: propose a hybrid: enable small delivery dedupe (last 8 event ids per session, TTL 5s) + add resume_overlap metric and console badge. Meanwhile restrict fast-handoff to non-multiplexed sessions.
Lin: implementable quickly. I can scope a change to only apply relaxed fast-handoff for single-stream sessions. For MPX, use strict accept (fast path disabled).
Gina: Team wants timeline: if we do hybrid, can we roll to canary in 30m?
Lin: yes. I'll add metric runtime.stream.resume_overlap and a proxy flag for dedupe buffer. Minimal proxy patch:```
--- a/proxy/delivery.go
+++ b/proxy/delivery.go
@@ -128,6 +128,14 @@ func deliverEvent(session, evt) {
  // existing delivery
+  if recentBuf.Contains(evt.ID) { 
+    metrics.Inc("runtime.stream.dedupe_drop")
+    return // avoid double delivery
+  }
+  recentBuf.Push(evt.ID, 5*time.Second)
+
  sendToClient(evt)
 }
```
Harper: I'll add a sampled trace collector to capture overlap cases (so we can later evaluate strict vs relaxed).
DeployBot: starting canary: runtime/routing/2026-04-08/hybrid-resume-dedupe -> eu-canary (id: d-10258).
DeployBot: canary finished: 6 instances updated, health checks OK.
Harper: initial canary metrics: runtime.stream.resume_overlap down from 0.38% -> 0.04% on canary hosts; dedupe_drop count=9 in 15m. Billing oddities reduced on sampled customers.
Mika (console): I'll add a small orange "handoff in progress" badge on route pages and surface the resume_overlap chart on the route diagnostics page. Low-risk UX change.
Gina: next steps: 1) Lin to file tradeoff doc for strict accept vs hybrid (latency vs correctness), 2) billing to confirm dedupe window acceptance, 3) keep canary for 4h then widen if stable.
Harper: repro harness + logs uploaded to gcs link. I'll follow-up with sampled traces and a quantitative compare of p99 handoff latency pre/post.
Lin: thanks. If the hybrid keeps duplicates low without raising tail drops we'll keep it; otherwise we'll reconvene on stricter sync.
Gina: thanks all. I'll coordinate status messaging if support tickets spike. :thumbsup:
